overview: After 1.Nh3 d5 2.g3 e5 White plays 3.f4, challenging the e5 pawn. If Black takes with 3...exf4 White regains with Nxf4, but in the most played line 3...Bxh3 4.Bxh3 exf4 5.O-O fxg3 6.hxg3 White is a pawn down for the bishop pair and open h-file (the Gent Gambit). The lines are unusual and little studied.

white_ideas.idea: Open lines on the kingside after f4
Use the h-file and bishop pair for attack

black_ideas.idea: Take on f4 and keep the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: Black centre pawns on d5 and e5

character.notes: Wild flank play with an exposed white king.

gambit.notes: After 4.Bxh3 exf4 5.O-O fxg3 6.hxg3 White is a pawn down; Black can keep it.

approach.notes: Almost never chosen by strong players.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...exf4 4.Nxf4
sublines_that_differ.how: White regains the pawn at once and material is level

character.reason: An exposed king and open files after the pawn sacrifice.

gambit.reason: The most played line leaves White a pawn down.

soundness.reason: White gets too little for the pawn.

plans.reason: White tries to use the open h-file.
